section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you turn left on a solid red light if not prohibited?
options: a:From a two-way street onto a one-way street after stopping,b:Under no circumstances,c:Onto any street if no vehicles or pedestrians are present
note: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn left on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street after coming to a complete stop and ensuring it is safe.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect your driving abilities?
options: a:They slow your reaction time, give a false sense of confidence, and impair thinking (all of the above),b:They only affect your mood,c:They improve coordination
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, slows reaction times, and reduces coordination and distance perception.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Perception and reaction time and braking distance.;b:Braking distance.;c:Reaction distance.;d:Steering ability.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. Steering ability is not a primary factor in stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle is headed toward you in your lane, what action should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
note: Honk to warn, steer right to escape if possible, and brake firmly and steadily to reduce impact if a collision seems unavoidable.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Excessive speed for conditions.,d:All of the above.
note: Inattentive driving, tailgating, and driving too fast for conditions are common causes of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow center lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.;b:To turn into a driveway or make a left turn when permitted.;c:To pass another car.;d:To change lanes for any reason.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing, but you may cross them to turn left into a driveway or to make other permitted left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe and legal.;b:Flash your lights to force the other driver to move over.;c:Use the road shoulder to pass.;d:Pass only if a police officer allows it.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires using the lane for oncoming traffic; only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,b:Shift to park.,c:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift into neutral, apply steady braking, pull off the roadway when safe, and turn off the engine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when approaching an intersection marked with a yield sign?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.;b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.;c:Yield only to traffic on your right.;d:Proceed because yield signs are suggestions only.
note: A yield sign means slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you plan to enter.

question: Why maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:To prevent other drivers from cutting you off,b:To allow time to react to unexpected situations,c:To keep traffic flowing faster
note: Keeping a space cushion gives you time to react and take evasive actions if other drivers make mistakes.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line indicates lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your interstate exit, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and use it to return,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn,b:Make a U-turn in the lane
note: Do not back up or make dangerous turns; proceed to the next exit to safely return to your intended route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which takes precedence over the others at an intersection?
options: a:A steady red light.;b:A police officer directing traffic.;c:A stop sign.;d:A flashing yellow light.
note: Directions from police officers or authorized traffic controllers override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings.

question: If an accident scene is not readily visible to oncoming traffic, you should:
options: a:Warn approaching drivers by having someone or using lights/flares to alert them,b:Let oncoming traffic watch out for themselves,c:Wait passively for police to arrive and handle warning
note: Warn approaching traffic to prevent further collisions using people, flashlights, or flares when safe to do so.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.,b:Tells you about traffic laws and regulations.,c:Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
note: Diamond-shaped signs with a yellow background and black symbols are warning signs that alert drivers to conditions on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When reversing your vehicle, what is the correct practice?
options: a:Rely only on mirrors to guide you.,b:Flash your lights while backing.,c:Open your door to look back.,d:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.
note: When backing, turn and look through the rear window; do not rely only on mirrors or sensors, and check for small children and obstacles.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.,d:Black.
note: Yellow centerlines are used to separate lanes of traffic traveling in opposite directions.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the left.;b:Keep driving normally.;c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop.;d:Slam on your brakes.
note: Grip the steering wheel firmly, release the accelerator to slow gradually, and steer to remain in your lane. When you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road to a safe place.

question: What does a solid yellow X over a traffic lane indicate?
options: a:Drivers must move out of the indicated lane because it is about to be used by oncoming traffic.,b:That drivers may drive regularly in the indicated lane.,c:That the indicated lane is for left turns only.
note: A solid yellow X is a lane control signal meaning the lane is about to be or is no longer available in your direction; move out of it safely.

question: What will help someone overcome the influence of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime,b:Hot coffee,c:Fresh air,d:Only the passage of time.
note: Nothing short of allowing time will reduce alcohol in the bloodstream and restore sobriety.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Use your parking lights only.,c:Use your headlights only.,d:Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low-beam headlights on.
note: If you stop at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so other road users can see your vehicle.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill.;b:In a parking lot.;c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.;d:Within 200 feet of a stop sign.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk nor in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: As a pedestrian, you should:
options: a:Walk facing traffic on the left side when no sidewalk exists and look for turning vehicles before crossing,b:Always insist on right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk,c:Run across streets to keep up with traffic flow
note: Pedestrians should walk facing traffic where no sidewalk exists, avoid running, and watch for turning vehicles before crossing.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs are typically white with black markings and must be obeyed.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or fall back until you are visible in their mirrors,b:Maintain your position in the blind spot,c:Flash your lights rapidly to get their attention
note: Avoid driving in another vehicle's blind spot; adjust speed slightly so they can see you in their mirrors.

question: Why must you be extra cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,d:Bicycles never signal their turns.
note: Passing drivers must be cautious because cyclists may swerve and oncoming vehicles may not expect you to enter the opposing lane to pass.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Ease off the gas, avoid immediate heavy braking, then gradually slow and pull off the road,b:Apply hard braking immediately,c:Continue at the same speed and steer to the shoulder
note: On a blowout, remove your foot from the accelerator, avoid hard braking until control is regained, then slow gently and pull off safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane closest to your original lane.,b:The middle lane regardless of position.,c:Any lane you choose after turning.,d:The farthest lane from your original lane.
note: When turning, enter the lane nearest to the lane you used before the turn and do not change lanes during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot,b:Only signal when other traffic is present,c:Rely solely on inside rearview mirror
note: Signal early, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive anyway; emotions won't change your ability.,b:Drive faster because you feel more alert.,c:Take time to focus and calm down before starting to drive.,d:Listen to loud music to distract yourself while driving.
note: Emotional states can impair driving ability; take time to calm down and concentrate before getting behind the wheel.

question: When loading a trailer, approximately what percentage of the trailer's weight should rest on the vehicle's hitch?
options: a:About 10 to 15 percent,b:Five percent,c:15 to 20 percent
note: About 10–15% of the trailer's total weight should be on the tow vehicle's hitch to ensure proper handling.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what is the appropriate warning action?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Wave your arms.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to warn other road users of an imminent collision or danger when they may not see you.

question: What is a frequent cause of many crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions.,b:Consistently checking mirrors.,c:Yielding the right-of-way.,d:Using turn signals too early.
note: Many crashes are caused by driving too fast for the conditions; slow down when conditions are unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When making a turn such as into a driveway or alley.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; they may be crossed when making a lawful turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
note: Only time will reduce BAC. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent the pass.;b:Slow down to make room in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass easily.;c:Maintain the same speed.;d:Move into the lane to the left without signaling.
note: Slow to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the passing maneuver safely and more quickly.

question: Bicyclists must refrain from:
options: a:Carrying passengers unless the bicycle is designed for them,b:Riding at night under any circumstances,c:Riding on any sidewalk anywhere
note: Bicyclists should not carry passengers unless the bike is equipped for it; sidewalk and nighttime rules vary by location and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions,b:The posted maximum speed limit only,c:Any speed you feel comfortable with
note: You must drive at speeds that are reasonable and prudent for the road, traffic, weather, and visibility, and within posted limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering and ensuring it is safe,b:After slowing to check for cross traffic,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
note: If there's no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when clear.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards,b:An upcoming school zone only,c:A public recreation area
note: Diamond-shaped signs (often yellow or orange) warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead.

question: Which color line divides lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Yellow centerlines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you allow the rider?
options: a:To share the shoulder with your vehicle.;b:Only half of a traffic lane.;c:A full lane so the motorcycle has room to maneuver.;d:To ride between lanes like a car.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle and is entitled to a full lane. Allow motorcyclists space to maneuver safely.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers others,b:Very uncommon and not concerning,c:Harmless if you are experienced
note: Distracted driving greatly increases the likelihood of crashes and endangers drivers, passengers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, how should you return to the pavement?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.;b:Stop on the edge of the road and then re-enter quickly.;c:Reduce speed without braking and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.;d:Accelerate and swerve back onto the road.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto a low shoulder, slow down without braking sharply and re-enter the roadway carefully, checking traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane,b:Pass with caution,c:Slow down immediately
note: A solid yellow line beside your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what should you do?
options: a:Stop at the scene.,b:Call law enforcement if required and check for injuries.,c:Provide help to injured persons.,d:All of the above.
note: Stop if possible, check for injuries and call police when there is injury, death, or sufficient property damage; report the crash as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to the right lane?
options: a:Immediately after passing regardless of distance.;b:Only when you intend to turn left.;c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed to move back safely.;d:After slowing down to below posted speed limit.
note: Return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to move back.

question: Which of the following is true about work zones?
options: a:They are marked with black and white signs.;b:They do not require drivers to slow down.;c:They may be stationary or involve moving operations and are marked with orange signs.;d:They are always stationary.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., striping crews) and are marked by orange signs with black letters or symbols. Slow down and pay extra attention.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Proceed normally through the intersection.,b:Stop and proceed when a green light appears.,c:Slow down and proceed with care.
note: A flashing yellow signal means caution: slow down, look, and proceed with care.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.;b:They can be ticketed.;c:They will always receive only a warning.;d:They must be escorted by law enforcement home.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be cited for violating traffic laws.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A steady red light.;b:A stop sign.;c:A yield sign.;d:A warning sign.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is most accurate?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,c:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.
note: Always make sure all passengers are properly restrained. Children 12 and under should ride in the rear seat; never place a rear-facing infant restraint in a front seat with an active airbag.

question: If you change your legal name, how long do you have to notify the county examiner of drivers?
options: a:Within 30 days,b:Within 60 days,c:Within 10 days
note: A change of name requires you to notify the county examiner of drivers and usually to appear in person with proof within 30 days of the change.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,b:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When safe, pull over to the side of the road to allow emergency vehicles a clear path to their destination.

question: If an emergency vehicle is directly behind you in heavy traffic and you cannot immediately clear a path, what should you do?
options: a:Force your way into the adjoining lane.;b:Stop immediately where you are.;c:Continue moving slowly until you can safely get out of the way and clear a path.;d:Blow your horn to hurry traffic.
note: When an emergency vehicle is behind you, continue to move slowly and clear a path as soon as it is safe to do so; do not force your way recklessly.

question: If a transit bus signals it is re-entering traffic after a stop, you must:
options: a:Yield to allow the bus to re-enter,b:Honk to warn the bus,c:Speed up to prevent delays
note: Yield to transit vehicles that are signaling to pull back onto the main roadway after loading or unloading so the bus can safely re-enter traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working signalized intersection, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic signal,b:Follow only the traffic lights,c:Honk to confirm directions
note: When an officer is directing traffic, their signals take precedence over traffic lights and signs.

question: If you strike an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.;b:Drive away after waiting two minutes.;c:Call a tow truck and leave without leaving information.;d:Report it only if the damage is extensive.
note: If you cannot locate the owner of an unattended vehicle you hit, leave a written notice with your contact information and a description of what happened.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to provide space,b:Stop immediately in your travel lane,c:Maintain speed and remain in your lane
note: If safe, change lanes away from stopped emergency vehicles; if you cannot, slow to a speed below the posted limit and give as much room as possible.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you can see the vehicle.;b:Pull to the curb and look to see if the emergency vehicle is coming down your street, then stop.;c:Slow down and keep moving in your lane until you spot it.;d:Speed up to clear the area.
note: If you hear an emergency siren nearby but cannot locate the vehicle, safely pull over to the right and stop until you are sure it is not headed toward you.

question: The space needed to cross traffic depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic,b:Whether a stop sign is present,c:Your use of turn signals
note: The gap required to cross traffic varies with road conditions, weather, and speed/distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: As a motorist, how should you treat bicyclists on the road?
options: a:Respect their rights and privileges as vehicle operators.,b:Allow a bicyclist twice as much room as you think they need.,c:Always give bicyclists the right-of-way when crossing a bike lane.,d:Expect bicyclists to stay out of vehicle lanes.
note: Bicyclists are legally considered vehicle operators and deserve the same respect and rights; give them adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head (blind spots at the sides and rear).;b:Directly behind your vehicle only.;c:You can see in your rearview mirror.;d:Directly under your vehicle.
note: Blind spots are areas beside and behind the vehicle that cannot be seen using mirrors alone; move your head to check them.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow for your lane, you may:
options: a:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians still in the intersection,b:Stop and then proceed only if signaled by an officer,c:Proceed without regard for other traffic
note: A steady green arrow gives you the protected movement, but yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a crowded freeway, you should:
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed and check mirrors/blind spots before merging,b:Pull immediately onto the freeway and force traffic to yield,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap
note: Use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway before merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who may proceed first?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver on the left.,d:The driver with the largest vehicle.
note: At four-way stops, the first vehicle to stop at the intersection has the right to proceed first.

question: A correctly adjusted seat belt should be:
options: a:Buckled snugly across hip bones and lower abdomen,b:Loose for comfort,c:Hidden under the seat
note: Lap belts should rest snugly across the hip bones; shoulder belts should lie across the chest for proper protection.

question: What must you do when approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,b:Continue driving when you think most kids are probably done exiting the bus.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, you are required to stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Turning on your car radio.,b:Slowing down.,c:Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
note: Schedule regular breaks to rest and stretch to prevent drowsiness while driving long distances.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time and increases the chance of a rear-end collision if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the rearview mirror.;b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.;c:Look into the left side mirror only.;d:Flash your headlights to notify others.
note: To check blind spots, glance over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move to ensure no vehicle is hidden from your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps should you take just before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,c:Check your rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic and then glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, you should:
options: a:Familiarize yourself with the controls (lights, wipers, horn, etc.) before driving,b:Ignore minor defects to avoid embarrassment,c:Drive immediately without checking anything
note: Take a few minutes to locate and test lights, signals, wipers, brakes, and other controls, and correct any obvious defects before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked with double solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:To make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:To pass another vehicle if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never under any circumstances.,d:To overtake a slow vehicle at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do advisory speed or speed restriction signs indicate about driving speeds?
options: a:They can be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.;b:They show a recommended speed for a curve or condition but you must drive slower in poor conditions.;c:They are triangular in shape.;d:They are blue signs with black lettering.
note: Advisory speed signs show recommended speeds for specific conditions such as curves. If weather or road conditions are poor, reduce speed below the advisory speed.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: How should you look ahead to prepare for things that may happen on the road?
options: a:Continuously scan the entire roadway and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Keep your left foot resting on the brake.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Actively scanning far ahead and at the sides helps you detect and prepare for hazards before they become emergencies.

question: If you drive a heavy truck or bus, what responsibility do you have toward other highway users?
options: a:You can expect smaller vehicles to always stay out of your way.;b:You may use the extra size of your vehicle to advantage in traffic.;c:You must consider the limitations of your vehicle and give proper consideration to others.;d:You are exempt from yielding in tight situations.
note: Drivers of large vehicles must be aware of their vehicles' limitations and give proper consideration to other highway users, passengers, and cargo.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Talking or texting on a cell phone,b:Changing lanes quickly,c:Driving with high beams on
note: Many activities distract drivers, including phone use, eating, and adjusting controls. Avoid non-driving tasks while behind the wheel.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest method to pass a bicyclist going the same direction?
options: a:Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with ample space,b:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign,c:Continue straight; the bicyclist must get out of your way
note: Pass bicyclists like other vehicles but give at least 3 feet clearance (more at higher speeds) and avoid startling them with horns or close passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To make a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:As close to the right side of the road as possible,b:Near the center of the street,c:Close to the left side of the street
note: Before turning right, move as far to the right as practicable and avoid cutting across lanes while turning.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.;b:There is a larger volume of traffic after dark.;c:Drivers cannot see as well at night.;d:Headlights make roads slippery.
note: Darkness reduces visibility. Use headlights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise or whenever people or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot,b:Only check your side mirror and then move,c:Rely solely on your rearview mirror
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to ensure it is clear; signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light means:
options: a:You may drive through the intersection if the road is clear,b:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic,c:You must slow and prepare to stop
note: A steady green allows you to proceed through the intersection if clear; when turning you must yield to other traffic and pedestrians as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you display your turn signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: a:At least 100 feet,b:At least 50 feet,c:At least 75 feet
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signaling earlier is recommended at higher speeds.

question: Which of the following helps prevent crashes?
options: a:Communicating your intentions to others (signals, horn when needed),b:Ignoring other drivers completely,c:Driving only on side streets
note: Communicate with other road users by signaling, using lights, or sound when necessary so others can anticipate your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Speeding can kill.
note: Both driving too slowly and speeding can be dangerous; driving at speeds inappropriate for conditions increases crash risk.

question: You are near a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. In which of the following situations must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted at the crossing.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.,d:All of the above.
note: Stop when a stop sign is present, a gate is lowered, flashing red lights are active, a flagger signals, or a train is visible or too close to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a sign does not prohibit it, what may you do at a solid red light?
options: a:Turn right after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.,b:Turn right at any time.,c:Never turn right.
note: Unless a sign prohibits right turns on red, you may turn right after coming to a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and turn around safely,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder,c:Make a quick lane change and exit from the next lane
note: Do not back up or make unsafe maneuvers on freeways; proceed to the next exit to safely return or reroute.

question: What should you do if other drivers around you are behaving angrily?
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid eye contact,b:React with hand gestures to discourage them,c:Try to match their speed to get away quickly
note: Physically and mentally distance yourself from angry drivers: avoid eye contact, do not engage, and move away safely.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when safe to do so.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is not allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you signal before making a turn or lane change?
options: a:At least 100 feet,b:At least 50 feet,c:At least 75 feet
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signal earlier at higher speeds to give others notice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.,c:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
note: At intersections of similar roads without signs or signals, you must yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion while driving?
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.;b:Only to your left and right.;c:Only in front of your vehicle.;d:On all sides of your vehicle to allow time to react to hazards.
note: Keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle to give yourself time to react and to avoid collisions.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions make driving less than perfect.,b:When you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a highway.,d:Never, unless posted speed is lower.
note: If visibility or road conditions are impaired, or anything makes driving less than perfect, reduce speed below the posted limit.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:More dangerous,b:No more or less dangerous,c:Less dangerous
note: Driving at night is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from headlights, and a higher likelihood of fatigued or impaired drivers on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through regardless.;b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through carefully.;c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.;d:Immediately make a U-turn.
note: A solid yellow light warns the signal will turn red. Stop if you can do so safely; if not, proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: A solid yellow arrow displayed by traffic signals means:
options: a:Prepare to stop — it has the same meaning as a circular yellow light,b:You may turn at your discretion without slowing,c:The arrow indicates nothing special
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turn phase is ending and drivers should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Anything that forces you to ____ can lead to a crash. Which completes the sentence?
options: a:Take your attention away from driving,b:Take your eyes off the road,c:Take your hands off the wheel
note: Anything that causes you to take your attention away from driving, take your eyes off the road, or take your hands off the wheel is a distraction and can cause a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are out due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.;b:Yield to other drivers as you would at a four-way stop, and proceed when it is your turn.;c:Park and wait for power to be restored.;d:Use hand signals instead of stopping.
note: Treat an intersection with no signals like a four-way stop: yield in the order that drivers arrive and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward is signaling what?
options: a:Turn left.;b:Stop or slowing down.;c:Turn right.;d:Prepare to speed up.
note: A left arm and hand pointing down indicates the driver intends to stop or slow. Adjust your driving accordingly.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.;b:Only when exiting an expressway.;c:Only when following a motorcycle.;d:Never increase following distance.
note: Increase following distance when a large vehicle blocks your view, in bad weather, heavy traffic, behind motorcycles or bicycles, or if someone is tailgating you.

question: At a light rail intersection you should always:
options: a:Look both ways before crossing and obey all traffic signals,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates,c:Assume trains yield to vehicles
note: Never drive around lowered gates; always look both ways before turning across tracks and obey all signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots,b:Always use cruise control at all times,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired
note: Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to confirm blind spot clearance before changing lanes on an interstate.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before moving on?
options: a:Wait until the children wave to you.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.,d:Pass the bus slowly without scanning.
note: After a school bus has activated its stop signals, watch carefully for children near the roadway before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when turning left.;b:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and when pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.;c:Only when driving faster than 35 mph.;d:Only in urban areas.
note: Use your turn signals for any left or right movement: lane changes, entering traffic from a parking spot or alley, and when turning.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:A special speed zone.;b:The area around the vehicle where drivers' stereos must be lowered.;c:The blind spots around a truck or bus where smaller vehicles cannot be seen.;d:A designated passenger loading area.
note: The 'No zone' refers to the blind spots around large vehicles (sides, rear, front) where smaller vehicles may not be visible to the truck or bus driver.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, what happens to your driving abilities?
options: a:Your reactions speed up.;b:You feel less confident overall.;c:Your reactions slow and you make more errors.;d:Your body metabolizes alcohol faster.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, increases overconfidence, and leads to more driving errors as BAC rises.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when the line between lanes is a ____ line.
options: a:Broken white,b:Solid yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and may be crossed to pass when it's safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you near an intersection, your best action is to:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so,b:Speed up to beat the red light,c:Apply brakes sharply to stop immediately in the center of the intersection
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon be red; prepare to stop if you can do so safely rather than rushing through.

question: What does a downward-facing triangular traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:Construction zone ahead.;b:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.;c:School crossing ahead.;d:No parking zone.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs. Slow down and yield to traffic or pedestrians when required.

question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:
options: a:Slow down and give as much space as possible,b:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass,c:Honk to alert the bicyclist just before passing
note: Pass bicyclists slowly and with ample lateral clearance; never crowd or surprise them with horns or close passes.

question: How much alcohol can begin to impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?
options: a:Only a BAC over the legal limit.,b:Alcohol does not affect these skills.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol.,d:Only heavy consumption over several drinks.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory, and impair driving ability.

question: When approaching a heavy truck uphill from the rear, what should you be aware of?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed.,b:You can always pass the truck safely uphill.,c:The truck will always move over for faster traffic.,d:The truck must stop for you if you honk.
note: Large vehicles often slow when climbing hills; expect reduced speed and avoid unsafe passing on hills with limited visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal light requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk,b:Slow down and proceed if clear,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present
note: A red light requires stopping before the intersection, any stop line, and crosswalk to ensure safety and compliance.

question: What should you do when driving on major highways to avoid highway hypnosis?
options: a:Stay alert.,b:Keep your eyes moving.,c:Be ready to react to road hazards.
note: Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be prepared to react to unexpected hazards to avoid highway hypnosis.

question: What is true about renewing an expired driver license in Hawaii?
options: a:You may drive during a 90-day grace period.,b:You may renew your license within six months of expiration.,c:You may renew within a year and still drive with the expired license.
note: In Hawaii, a license is void after its expiration; you must renew it. Renewal is available within a limited period before or after expiration but you may not legally drive with an expired license.

question: What is important to remember about driving on wet pavement?
options: a:That pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:To give yourself additional space when coming to a stop.,c:That wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
note: Road surfaces can be especially slippery just after rain begins. Slow down when roads are wet and give yourself extra stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles on the right and be prepared to slow or stop by covering the brake,b:Maintain speed and proceed regardless,c:Always stop even if clear
note: At uncontrolled intersections yield to the right when arriving simultaneously and be ready to brake or yield to avoid collisions.

question: You may not pass from either direction where the centerline is:
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:A single broken yellow,c:A combination of solid and dashed yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is prohibited from either direction.

question: If you're still upset after an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and cool off,b:Play loud music to distract yourself,c:Drive fast to blow off steam
note: Drivers who are angry or emotionally upset should take time to calm down before driving to avoid impaired judgment and risky behavior.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones.;b:No passing zones.;c:Speed limits.;d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pennant-shaped signs indicate no passing zones; they warn drivers not to pass other vehicles in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:When you hear a siren or see flashing red/blue lights,b:Under no circumstances,c:Only when other vehicles yield
note: You must yield right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens by pulling over and stopping if necessary.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and it begins to lose traction, how should you apply the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.,d:Release the brake and reapply quickly.
note: With Anti-Lock Brakes press and hold the brake firmly; ABS will automatically modulate braking to maintain control.

question: If you discover a defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible,b:Drive more slowly until you can afford the repair,c:Postpone repair until the vehicle is inconvenient to use
note: Any defect that affects safe operation should be corrected immediately before driving the vehicle.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcyclists have?
options: a:Half the width of a lane,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles,c:Only the bicycle lane
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane, just like other motor vehicles.

question: If another driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely,b:Pull alongside and yell at them,c:Flash your high beams repeatedly
note: To avoid road rage and reduce crash risk, don't react aggressively; let the incident pass and drive safely.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side-by-side, what must you do after one train passes?
options: a:Always proceed because the other track will be clear.;b:Come to a complete stop before crossing regardless.;c:Look for another approaching train on the other track before you proceed.;d:Drive faster to clear the second track quickly.
note: When multiple tracks exist, wait and check for trains on all tracks after one train passes before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should do what?
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way.;b:Yield to drivers already on the public road and merge when safe.;c:Force their way into traffic if necessary.;d:Drive at full speed to merge quickly.
note: If entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to vehicles already on the public road and merge safely when there is a gap.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop,b:Proceed normally,c:Take the right-of-way
note: Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to prevent injury to blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle arrive at the same time and the other vehicle is on your right, you should:
options: a:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right,b:Speed up and beat the other car through the intersection,c:Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light changes or you are otherwise permitted to go,b:Proceed if no other vehicles are present,c:Slow and proceed cautiously without stopping
note: A steady red light means stop; you may turn on red only where permitted after a full stop and when the way is clear.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has no signals or gates?
options: a:Always stop completely.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop after checking both directions.,c:Assume no trains use the crossing.,d:Drive across quickly without looking.
note: At unmarked crossings slow down, check both directions for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.

question: For drivers 21 and older, at what minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.08 percent,b:0.05 percent,c:0.02 percent
note: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

question: A person's driving ability can be impaired by:
options: a:Alcohol, medications, or lack of sleep,b:Only alcohol,c:Only illegal drugs
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness; all can reduce reaction and judgment.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what is your first responsibility?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Help the injured.,c:Call the police.
note: If involved in a crash, stop immediately, move to safety if possible, call the police and emergency services if needed, and render aid without moving seriously injured persons.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.;b:Pull up even with the car in front of the space before beginning to back in.;c:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.;d:Back into the space without aligning with the car ahead.
note: After finding a space, check traffic and signal, then stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning the parking maneuver.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Proceed like a stop sign and then go.;b:Stop and wait for a green light.;c:Slow down and proceed with caution.;d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, yielding as necessary.

question: Of the vehicle, the environment, and the driver, which is the most important factor in any driving situation?
options: a:The driver,b:The environment,c:The vehicle
note: Every driving situation involves the vehicle, the environment, and the driver; only the driver can evaluate conditions and apply skills, knowledge, and judgment to act safely.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause which of these conditions while driving?
options: a:Excessive engine noise only,b:You to become drowsy or suffer carbon monoxide exposure,c:Immediate engine stalling only
note: A leaky exhaust can allow toxic fumes, such as carbon monoxide, to enter the vehicle and can make occupants drowsy or even cause poisoning.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:At any time without checking.;b:Only during daylight hours.;c:When it is safe to change lanes.;d:Only to pass motorcycles.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights (use low beams),b:Use your parking lights only,c:Use your four-way flashers while driving
note: Turn on your headlights (low beam) at dusk or when visibility is reduced; dim to low beams within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: On slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Slow down and possibly drive below the posted limit,b:Drive faster to maintain control,c:Drive the posted speed limit regardless
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet and drive slower than the posted limit if conditions require.

question: Why should you avoid having a few drinks before driving home from work?
options: a:It helps you avoid rush hour traffic.,b:It relieves tension and makes you a safer driver.,c:It should be avoided because it can make you a dangerous driver.,d:It has no effect on driving ability.
note: Alcohol impairs reflexes, judgment, alertness, and vision; any amount can make driving unsafe.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Directly at the oncoming headlights.,b:Straight ahead in the center of your lane.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming drivers fail to dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road and use the markings to guide you rather than staring at the lights.

question: How does alcohol affect you when consumed on an empty stomach?
options: a:It is absorbed and affects you more rapidly,b:It affects you more slowly than when you have eaten,c:It has no different effect than on a full stomach
note: Alcohol is absorbed faster on an empty stomach and will affect you more quickly and intensely than after eating.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Keep physically fit and get regular checkups.,b:Know how any medicine you take affects driving.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above.
note: Maintain fitness, understand medication effects on driving, and only drive when you are physically capable.

question: What is a \No zone\" in relation to large vehicles?"
options: a:The large blind spots around trucks where cars disappear from the driver's view,b:A legal no passing zone,c:A one-way traffic area
note: \No zones\" are the extensive blind spots around trucks and large vehicles; avoid lingering in these areas where the driver cannot see you."

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, what is a good practice?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Keep driving but roll down the windows periodically.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.,d:Drink coffee and continue driving.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop at least every two hours for a break; if drowsy, park in a safe place and rest.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommendation that directly promotes safer night driving while operating your vehicle?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean to improve visibility.;b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.;c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.;d:Avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights.
note: While a flashlight can help in emergencies, it does not directly improve driving visibility at night. Keeping windows clean and avoiding glare are direct driving recommendations.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has no gates or flashing signals?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train and ensure the track is clear.,d:Assume the tracks are clear if you do not hear a train.
note: When no gates/signals are present, be prepared to yield and only cross when the entire vehicle can clear the tracks safely.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:You should come to a complete stop,c:You should merge into a lane in the arrow's direction
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: If a police officer asks you to take a chemical alcohol test, what must you do?
options: a:Do not have to take the test if you can prove that you weren’t drinking,b:Do not have to take the test if you have not violated any traffic rule.,c:Must take the test or risk losing your license.
note: In Hawaii, implied consent laws require drivers to submit to chemical testing when requested; refusal results in license revocation for a minimum period.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which of these should you NOT fail to do?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.;b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intention.;c:Check over your shoulder for other vehicles in your blind spot.;d:Ignore traffic beside you if mirrors look clear.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal your intentions, and look over your shoulder for vehicles that may be in your blind spot. Do not ignore traffic beside you.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.;b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.;c:Firmly slam on the brakes.;d:Shift into neutral.
note: On slippery surfaces, first remove your foot from the accelerator to reduce speed. If needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It decreases BAC quickly.;b:It cancels the effects of alcohol.;c:It has no effect on BAC and does not sober you up.;d:It speeds up how fast your body metabolizes alcohol.
note: Drinking coffee may make you feel more alert but does not reduce BAC or make you sober. Only time eliminates alcohol from your system.

question: Which color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Red lines.;b:White lines.;c:Yellow lines.;d:Blue lines.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the roadway. Broken white lines may be crossed to pass.

question: Why must you be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see,b:They rarely use headlights,c:Motorcyclists are less skilled than car drivers
note: Motorcycles are smaller, often hidden in blind spots, and harder to judge for speed and distance, so exercise extra caution around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign,b:The reduced speed applies only after the next sign,c:You have plenty of distance to slow down before the reduced zone
note: 'Reduced speed' signs indicate that the new speed limit begins at the sign; slow to the posted limit where indicated.

question: How is an arrogant driver typically described?
options: a:Someone purposely in a hurry and competing with other traffic.,b:A driver who shows little respect for traffic laws and others.,c:A driver you should try to avoid while driving.,d:All of the above.
note: An arrogant driver is often hurried, competitive, disrespectful of rules and others; avoid engaging with such drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When merging, accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping,b:That you are making a turn,c:That your emergency brake is engaged
note: Brake lights indicate to following drivers that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order for safety.

question: Which device increases crash risk when used by drivers?
options: a:CD player.,b:Radio.,c:Cell phone.,d:Hands-free intercom.
note: Using a cell phone is a major source of driver distraction and increases crash risk, even when hands-free.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for others to know your plans.,b:Just as you begin to change lanes.,c:After you change lanes.,d:Signal only if traffic is heavy.
note: Always signal early enough so other drivers understand your intent before you start the pass or lane change.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Lowing your ability to focus on driving.,b:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:Decreasing your chances of an accident.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce your ability to concentrate on driving tasks and increase the risk of a crash.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help.,b:Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: Signal before carefully exiting, turn on hazard flashers, get as far off the road as possible, and raise your hood to indicate a disabled vehicle.

question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic moves.,b:Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,d:Back up to make room.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Proceed.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.,d:Stop immediately at the line.
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light is about to appear; slow and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: When approaching railroad tracks you should:
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop,b:Speed up to cross before any gate comes down,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate
note: Approach tracks cautiously: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop for trains or track vehicles.

question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use parking lights.
note: In rain, use low-beam headlights so you can see and be seen without creating excessive glare.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Using proper turn signals.,c:Obeying posted speed limits.
note: Allowing extra travel time, using signals, and obeying speed limits all help reduce stress and the likelihood of road rage.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough to create a danger, you must not cross the tracks until it has completely passed, even if no signals are present or they are not working.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.,b:It is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Directed to do so by a flagger.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when gates are down, flashing red lights are operating, a stop sign is present, or when directed by a flagger.

question: What factor strongly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Signal lights.;b:The condition of the road surface.;c:The time of day.;d:The color of your vehicle.
note: Stopping distance is greatly affected by road conditions. Reduce speed when roads are slippery or otherwise hazardous.

question: All vehicle headlights must be working and properly aimed:
options: a:At all times,b:Only when driving in a city,c:Only on freeways
note: Headlights must be functional and properly adjusted whenever your vehicle is operated, especially at night or in poor visibility.

question: When should safety belts be worn?
options: a:Should be worn only when traveling at high speeds.,b:Should be worn at all times when driving or riding in a vehicle.,c:Should be worn loosely.
note: Safety belts must be worn at all times by drivers and passengers to reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should end up in which lane?
options: a:The lane nearest to the left side of the one-way street (left lane),b:The right lane of the street,c:The center of the street
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from (the left lane).

question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,c:Stop with part of your vehicle on the roadway.,d:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway when entering from a driveway or private road.

question: On an undivided roadway, when may you pass a school bus?
options: a:Under no circumstances.;b:Only when the bus's red warning lights are flashing.;c:When the bus's red warning lights are not flashing.;d:Only if the bus is stopped to let students off on the opposite side.
note: You may pass a school bus on an undivided road only if the bus's red warning lights are not flashing. When red lights flash, stop for the bus.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:If you lose control and need to alert others,b:When passing another car for routine reasons,c:To express anger
note: Use your horn to warn others of imminent danger, such as when you lose control; avoid using it for non-emergency or aggressive reasons.

question: If stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must produce:
options: a:Their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance,b:Only their license,c:Only proof of insurance
note: When stopped, a driver is responsible for showing a valid license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance upon request.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass,b:Retaliate by tailgating them,c:Cut them off to slow them down
note: Stay calm, create distance between you and the aggressive driver, avoid eye contact or gestures, and let them pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but no stop line or crosswalk is painted, where should you stop?
options: a:You are not required to stop.;b:Stop at a point nearest the roadway where you can safely see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.;c:Stop in the intersection to get a better view.;d:Stop where you can see at least 500 feet in both directions.
note: Stop at the nearest point before entering the roadway where you can see cross traffic. Do not enter the intersection to improve your view.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: When towing, where should the trailer's safety chain be attached on the towing vehicle?
options: a:To the frame of the towing vehicle,b:To the vehicle's bumper,c:To the trailer's hitch only
note: Safety chains must be attached between the trailer and the frame of the towing vehicle; they should not be connected solely to the bumper.

question: What should you do before driving into an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your route in advance,b:Depend entirely on road signs while driving,c:Have only a general idea of the destination
note: Plan your trip before you start driving so you know major turns and landmarks and can avoid unnecessary distractions while behind the wheel.

question: A good defensive driver:
options: a:Anticipates actions of other drivers and watches for hazards,b:Drives slowly at all times,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions
note: Defensive driving means anticipating others' actions, staying alert, and adapting speed and position to conditions.

question: When must you stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is stopped in your lane.,b:Only if you see children outside the bus.,c:When its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.,d:Never, if you are on the opposite side of the road.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and extends its stop arm.

question: Which factors affect your vehicle's braking distance?
options: a:The vehicle's speed.,b:Condition of brakes and tires.,c:Condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is influenced by speed, brake and tire condition, and pavement condition among other factors.

question: What is the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:An orange reflective triangle bordered in red,b:A rectangular red sign,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle (often with a red border) and indicates vehicles traveling 25 mph or slower.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat.;b:Your rearview mirror.;c:The steering wheel.;d:Your radio.
note: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see clearly; then adjust mirrors and the steering wheel as needed.

question: Combining drugs with alcohol will:
options: a:Increase your risk of causing a crash,b:Reduce alcohol's effect on driving,c:Be no more dangerous than alcohol alone
note: Drugs — illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter — can impair driving; combining them with alcohol increases crash risk.

question: An \End school zone\" sign notifies drivers that:"
options: a:The reduced school zone speed limit has ended,b:A 20 mph limit begins,c:You are entering a school area
note: The \End school zone\" sign indicates you've left the reduced-speed school zone and may resume the regular posted speed."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light you must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection,b:Maintain your normal speed and turn immediately,c:Stop and wait for a police officer's instruction
note: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn on a steady green, but you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To indicate what a driver must or must not do,b:To warn of hazards ahead,c:To provide information about nearby services
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do in specific areas, such as speed limits or turn restrictions.

question: What does a painted arrow in a lane usually indicate?
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow,b:The arrow is decorative and may be ignored,c:Drivers should always stop before following the arrow
note: Arrows painted in a lane indicate that drivers in that lane are required to make the movement shown by the arrow when it is safe to do so.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Stop and treat it like a stop sign,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present,c:Continue because they have the right-of-way
note: Flashing red lights indicate the driver must come to a full stop, then proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Signal in advance, slow gradually, move into the left lane when appropriate, and watch for oncoming vehicles/pedestrians,b:Speed up and turn quickly,c:Ignore rearview checks
note: Signal 3–5 seconds before turning, slow down, position in the left lane if required, and yield to traffic and pedestrians.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to which of these?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A yield sign,c:The signal is broken
note: A flashing red traffic signal requires a full stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceeding only when safe — same as a stop sign.

question: \Highway hypnosis\" can result from:"
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning,b:Frequent rest stops,c:Getting extra sleep before a trip
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when drivers stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, leading to micro-sleeps and reduced reaction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended upward indicates what maneuver?
options: a:The driver plans to turn left.;b:The driver plans to turn right.;c:The driver plans to stop.;d:The driver plans to accelerate.
note: A left arm extended upward signals the driver's intention to turn right. Be aware when following such a vehicle.

question: What is the meaning of a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution.

question: Round traffic signs generally warn drivers of what ahead?
options: a:No passing zones.;b:School zones.;c:Railroad crossings.;d:Stop signs.
note: Round signs typically indicate an upcoming railroad crossing area; use extra caution when approaching.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Turn on your windshield wipers,c:Turn on your headlights
note: Your first response to decreased visibility should be to slow down; also use headlights and wipers as appropriate.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of you. What should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
note: Always slow down and be prepared to stop when pedestrians are crossing; yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.;b:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.;c:Drive slower than surrounding traffic.;d:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers go much faster or slower than the surrounding traffic. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren on, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Slow down and remain in your lane.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Accelerate to clear the way faster.
note: You must immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.;b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.;c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.;d:You may pass at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited in both directions. You may cross only to turn left into a driveway or permitted location.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They follow different traffic laws than cars.,c:They always have the right-of-way.,d:They travel faster than cars.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and may have less visibility or lighting, so drivers should be especially vigilant.

question: In which conditions does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On paved highways.;b:When driving at night.;c:On wet or icy roads.;d:When driving on straight, level roads.
note: Stopping distances increase significantly on wet, icy, or loose surfaces; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:The person driving the car.,b:Passengers when they are on a long drive.,c:All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts at all times; an unbelted passenger can become a projectile in a crash.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what is a reliable way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.;b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.;c:Take a cold shower to sober up.;d:Wait five minutes after your last drink and then drive carefully.
note: Arrange a ride with someone who has not been drinking. Coffee or showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
