question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.;b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.;c:Flash your headlights to let other drivers know you're turning.;d:Turn off your signal to avoid confusing others.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so that if another vehicle hits you from behind you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a multi-lane roadway, you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if safe,b:Honk at incoming traffic,c:Always maintain your current speed regardless of others
note: On multi-lane roads, move over or make room for vehicles merging into traffic if it is safe to do so.

question: As a pedestrian, you should:
options: a:Not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching,b:Always insist on right-of-way at all times,c:Enter a crosswalk anytime because vehicles must stop
note: Even though pedestrians have rights, do not enter crossings if vehicles are approaching and may not be able to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Coming to an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear,b:Slow and drive through if no cars are visible,c:Wait for a flashing green light
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop, yielding as needed, then proceeding when safe.

question: If faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should:
options: a:Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist to avoid handling two hazards at once,b:Split the difference and pass between them,c:Pull onto the shoulder immediately
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: allow the oncoming car to pass, then safely pass the bicyclist when there's enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When your traffic signal is a green arrow,b:When entering a street from a garage or alley,c:When they are on a road to your left and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time
note: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage, and yield to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:Beer impairs less than wine.;b:Wine impairs less than beer.;c:The type of beverage does not change impairment; amount consumed matters.;d:Hard ciders and mixed drinks impair more than straight spirits always.
note: Impairment depends on how much alcohol enters the bloodstream, not on the beverage type. Amount and time are the key factors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When pulling forward from a driveway, what must you do regarding the sidewalk?
options: a:Have the right-of-way over pedestrians in the sidewalk area.,b:Must slow down before crossing the sidewalk area.,c:Must come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk area.
note: When driving out of a driveway, stop before entering the road and before crossing the sidewalk area; failing to stop is unlawful.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
note: Before turning or changing lanes, glance over your shoulder in the direction of your move to check blind spots; do not rely on mirrors alone.

question: What does an orange-colored roadway sign generally indicate?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.
note: Orange signs with black symbols are typically used for construction, maintenance, and emergency operations.

question: Guide signs that provide direction and mileage are usually which color?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Guide signs (destination/directional signs) are typically green with white lettering and show directions and distances.

question: When you hear a siren behind you while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Slow down, then pull over to the right and stop when safe.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Continue driving normally.
note: You should reduce speed safely and pull to the right to allow the emergency vehicle to pass; if trapped in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can clear a path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, who must you slow for and yield to?
options: a:Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: You must slow and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout before entering.

question: Alcohol consumption causes:
options: a:Impaired concentration, coordination, and slowed judgment,b:Improved coordination,c:No effect on driving ability
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even if no traffic is visible,b:Signal only if visible traffic is present,c:Signal only at night
note: Always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from the curb; do not skip signaling even if you think no one is around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two‑lane road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,b:Maintain your slow speed until the traffic clears,c:Prevent other cars from passing you
note: If your speed is impeding traffic on a two-lane, two-way road, pull off the roadway and let vehicles pass.

question: Which are the most effective safety restraints in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Wearing a lap and shoulder belt plus having a properly functioning airbag provides the best protection in a front-end collision.

question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or OTC medicine?
options: a:The medicine will cancel out the alcohol.,b:The alcohol helps the medicine work better.,c:The combination can multiply impairing effects.,d:There is no interaction between alcohol and medicines.
note: Alcohol combined with medications can increase impairment, sometimes making the effects much stronger than either alone.

question: Most of the information you need to drive safely comes primarily from which sense?
options: a:Seeing,b:Hearing,c:Touch
note: Nearly all the information needed to drive safely is obtained visually; maintain constant awareness of conditions ahead and around your vehicle.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver,c:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street, even if the pedestrian is not obeying signals or is otherwise careless; be prepared to stop to prevent injury.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line when:
options: a:Doing so would interfere with traffic,b:Turning left into a driveway,c:When the car ahead is disabled
note: A single broken line may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: A driver ahead is distracted by passengers and driving with one hand. How should you respond?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Avoid following the driver's example.,c:Know that the driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.
note: If another driver is distracted, give them extra space because their risk of an accident is increased.

question: Must traffic signs and pavement markings be obeyed?
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings regulate traffic flow and must always be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,d:Leave wheels in any position if parking brake is set.
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

question: Which statement about bicyclists is correct?
options: a:Bicyclists may ride side-by-side on roadways.;b:Bicyclists may ride two abreast on bike paths or lanes except where signs prohibit it.;c:Bicyclists always have right-of-way over pedestrians.;d:Bicyclists must always ride on the sidewalk.
note: On roadways bicyclists must ride single file, but they may ride two abreast on bike lanes or paths where it does not impede traffic and signs do not prohibit it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Follow what surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger,c:Ignore the flagger because signs control traffic
note: You are legally required to obey directions from flaggers in work zones for safety of workers and drivers.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.;b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.;c:The reduced noise of large vehicles.;d:The ability to pass the truck at any time.
note: Large trucks require more distance to stop; other drivers should allow for these increased stopping distances and avoid lingering in blind spots.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding,b:Go through as soon as one train passes,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train
note: When stopped at multi-track crossings, wait until you can see down all tracks and are sure no other trains are approaching before crossing.

question: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights and approaches, what should you do?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: Yield the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using lights and sirens; where possible, pull to the right and stop until they pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Night drives,c:Slow speeds
note: Higher speeds dramatically increase stopping distances and the force of impact, increasing the severity of crashes.

question: Which is a key practice for driving safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,c:Not drive if you are tired.
note: At night, reduce speed, increase your following distance, and ensure your headlights are functioning to improve safety.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving,b:It helps cars behind you move faster,c:You will need extra space to open your door
note: Allow more space when stopped uphill because the car in front could roll back when traffic resumes.

question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp properly?
options: a:Slow down before entering the ramp.,b:Begin to slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,c:Keep the same speed while on the ramp.,d:Stop on the ramp to check directions.
note: Do not reduce speed until you are on the exit ramp; begin slowing after you have moved onto it and can safely do so.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Do not speed when the roads are wet and maintain good tire tread and pressure.;b:Spin the steering wheel quickly when water is felt.;c:Drive faster to cut through the water layer.;d:Deflate your tires slightly before heavy rain.
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by slowing down on wet roads and by maintaining proper tire pressure and tread depth.

question: When may you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Whenever you turn on your four-way flashers.,b:If no part of the vehicle is on the roadway.,c:To consult a map or ask directions.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except for emergencies; use flashers and move off the road only if necessary.

question: What can happen when alcohol and drugs are consumed together?
options: a:Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:Help cure your illness.
note: Combining alcohol and drugs can increase the impairing effects of both and makes driving more dangerous.

question: How must a driver treat pedestrians in the roadway?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if they are not legally entitled to it.;b:Only yield when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.;c:Make sure the pedestrian notices your vehicle before proceeding.;d:Yield only if a traffic light is present.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield the right-of-way to pedestrians even if they are crossing where they should not be.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings to warn of unexpected conditions.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: If an emergency vehicle is following you without lights or siren, you do not need to clear the road; continue driving normally.

question: Which statement about pavement lines is true?
options: a:White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.;b:White lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.;c:Yellow lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.;d:Red lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; only cross white lines when they are broken.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels frequently.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Snow tires can improve traction on slippery roads.
note: You should not use cruise control on snow, ice, or in similar hazardous conditions; this statement is not true.

question: When towing a trailer, which equipment should it definitely have?
options: a:Tires that are properly inflated.,b:Properly mounted and lubricated wheels covered with fenders or mud guards.,c:The proper lamps and reflectors.
note: A trailer should have properly inflated tires, properly mounted and lubricated wheels with fenders or mud guards, and must be equipped with appropriate lamps and reflectors.

question: You should always signal when you are:
options: a:Changing lanes,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area
note: Signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of parking spaces, or entering traffic from an alley or driveway to communicate your intentions.

question: When towing a loaded trailer that weighs more than half the towing vehicle or 3,000+ pounds, the trailer must have:
options: a:Brakes and breakaway protection,b:Only hub caps,c:No special equipment
note: Trailers over specified weights must be equipped with brakes and breakaway protection for safety and legal compliance.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, what should you remember?
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
note: Because of their size and weight, large trucks need more distance to stop and more room to maneuver.

question: How should you approach crossing railroad tracks safely?
options: a:Listen, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe,b:Look only when lights are flashing,c:Cross quickly when you hear a train in the distance
note: Before crossing railroad tracks, look and listen for approaching trains from both directions and obey signals and gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.;b:At your side mirror only.;c:Over your left shoulder.;d:At the road ahead only.
note: Look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes to the left.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:
options: a:Often have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle,b:Make no driving errors,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry
note: Eating or drinking distracts hands and eyes from driving and increases the risk of lane wander and errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning required?
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
note: You must signal your intentions in advance, usually at least 100 feet before turning, to inform other road users of your planned move.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Limit your driving to weekdays.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to reduce the chance of death or serious injury in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic?
options: a:Should leave room on your right for other vehicles to pass.,b:Must yield to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Must not cross any solid yellow line.
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and complete the turn only when it is safe.

question: What is the vertical order of lights on a traffic signal from top to bottom?
options: a:Red, green, yellow.,b:Red, yellow, green.,c:Green, yellow, red.
note: Vertically arranged traffic lights have red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver cuts you off?
options: a:Call the police immediately.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.
note: If cut off by an aggressive driver, remain calm and get out of their way rather than escalating the situation.

question: When driving at night and another vehicle is approaching, your headlights should be set to:
options: a:Low beam,b:High beam,c:Parking lights only
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following other vehicles; use low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: When you first turn the ignition on before starting the engine, instrument panel warning lamps should:
options: a:Illuminate briefly to show they are functioning,b:Remain off until the engine is running,c:Never illuminate unless there's a malfunction
note: Most warning lights light briefly when the key is turned to verify the lamps are functioning; a lamp that never lights may be faulty.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection,b:Stop but you may proceed if clear,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped until a green arrow or green light allows the movement.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means recognizing hazards and acting early to avoid crashes and conflicts with other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: When the light turns green, yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection before proceeding.

question: A good general rule regarding passing is:
options: a:Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Constantly try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic
note: Passing increases collision risk; follow traffic flow and only pass when safe and necessary within legal limits.

question: Why is driving at night more difficult than in daylight?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night,c:It is more likely to rain at night
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision and makes it harder to see hazards; drive at a speed that allows you to stop within your sight distance.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a multi-lane road signals:
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction where lane changes and passing are permitted,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is forbidden,c:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is forbidden
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and permit lane changes and passing when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving behind a slow vehicle on a four-lane highway, before changing lanes you must:
options: a:Make sure there is sufficient room in traffic, check blind spots, and signal at least 100 feet before moving,b:Only signal if someone is behind you,c:Change lanes immediately without signaling
note: Check conditions ahead and to the sides, confirm your blind spot is clear, and signal appropriately before changing lanes.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicates you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and be prepared to stop if necessary,b:Always come to a full stop, even when clear,c:Only slow down for emergency vehicles
note: A yield sign means you must slow as you approach and yield to vehicles or pedestrians; stop if conditions require it.

question: When stopped in traffic at a railroad crossing without gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.;b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.;c:There is enough room ahead for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks before you drive onto them.;d:You may stop on the tracks if necessary for traffic.
note: Ensure you have enough space to clear the tracks before driving onto them; never pass another vehicle while approaching or crossing railroad tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to continue carefully through an intersection on a yellow light?
options: a:If there are pedestrians crossing,b:If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane,c:If you are already turning right or already in the intersection
note: If a steady yellow light appears when you are already within the intersection, continue through carefully. Yield to pedestrians and emergency vehicles as required.

question: Which signal tells you to slow and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When it begins to rain and visibility is reduced, you should:
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed to keep traffic moving,c:Pull into the passing lane and stay there
note: Reduce speed and turn on headlights when visibility drops in rain; if visibility is severely reduced, safely pull off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper sequence to change lanes?
options: a:Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,b:Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
note: Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and change lanes only when safe.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow and a red light together, what does that mean?
options: a:You may only drive straight ahead.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You must wait for the solid green light to go in any direction.,d:You may turn in any direction with caution.
note: A green arrow with a red circular light means you may proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow, provided the intersection is clear.

question: What information do highway pavement markings provide?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Are only found in construction zones.,c:Provide information for drivers.
note: Pavement markings guide drivers on lane use, passing zones, and other important roadway information and must be obeyed.

question: What can happen when alcohol and another drug are combined?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased,b:No effect will occur,c:The combination will always reduce the effects of each
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment; even small amounts of alcohol with certain medications can have a strong combined effect.

question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:
options: a:Stop at or near the scene, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles,b:Leave immediately to avoid liability,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct cars around the wreck
note: You must stop after an accident, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions to reduce fire risk while awaiting help.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop,b:Always sound your horn when you see children,c:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not
note: Be alert for children at school crossings; yield and be prepared to stop when they are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, it's important to:
options: a:Signal ahead, check blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before entering,b:Only signal if other drivers are present,c:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors
note: Signal in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection,b:Speed up to clear the intersection,c:Continue as you have the right-of-way
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light is imminent; stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already within the intersection.

question: Which of these are used on some highways to direct drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:Flashing yellow lights.,c:White lines on the road shoulders.,d:Arrow markings or lane arrows.
note: Arrows or arrow markings on signs or pavement indicate which lanes are designated for turning or through travel.

question: If you are charged with DUI and refuse the required chemical test, what is a likely consequence?
options: a:You may lose your driver license for a minimum of 12 months because you refused the test.;b:You will only lose your license if convicted of DUI.;c:You will only lose your license for refusing if also convicted of another traffic offense.;d:Refusing the test has no administrative consequences.
note: Operating a vehicle in Hawaii is consent to BAC testing when requested. Refusal to submit to a chemical test results in automatic license revocation for at least one year.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid,b:Turn your wheel into oncoming traffic,c:Overcorrect sharply
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: If you must make a quick stop and your vehicle does not have ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal continuously.,b:Firmly pump the brake pedal.,c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,d:Shift into neutral and coast to a stop.
note: If no ABS is present, firmly pump the brakes to stop quickly while maintaining steering control.

question: When children ride in vehicles, they should:
options: a:Be properly secured in appropriate child seats or safety belts,b:Be safely held by a strong adult,c:Stand on the floor in the back seat
note: Children must be properly restrained in child safety seats or seat belts appropriate for their size and age; no adult can reliably hold them during a crash.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning,b:It increases tire wear,c:It reduces fuel efficiency only
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment; repair leaks promptly to prevent poisoning.

question: What is the proper lighting to use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:Hazard lights,c:High beams
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility further.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as possible and stop,b:Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane,c:Speed up to get out of the way quickly
note: On two-lane roads, immediately pull to the right and stop; do not block intersections and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that which light will soon appear?
options: a:Flashing yellow,b:Steady green,c:Steady red
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to change to red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Sharply away from the curb,b:Slightly to the right,c:Sharply toward the curb
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will rest against the curb and not into traffic. If no curb, turn toward edge of road.

question: If you must drive in foggy conditions, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.;b:Low beam headlights.;c:Parking lights only.;d:Hazard lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: If you change the address on your vehicle registration, you must:
options: a:Notify the County Department of Finance within 30 days,b:Notify the County Department of Finance only when selling the car,c:Wait until your next renewal to update it
note: You must notify the county examiner or appropriate department in writing within 30 days of an address change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopped in line at a stop sign and the vehicles ahead have cleared the intersection. If there is no cross traffic, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection without stopping again.;b:Come to a complete stop at the stop sign or line before proceeding.;c:Slowly roll past the stop sign if the road looks clear.;d:Honk to warn cross traffic before going.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a full stop and yield to any approaching traffic before proceeding past a stop sign.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It improves driving skills but impairs judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.,d:It sharpens perception in small amounts.
note: Alcohol degrades reaction time, vision, perception of speed and distance, and impairs judgment and decision making.

question: For a road test, the vehicle you provide must be:
options: a:In safe operating condition with required inspection and insurance,b:Owned by the testing agency,c:Allowed to have safety defects for the test
note: The vehicle used for a road test must be safe, free of defects, with current inspection and insurance documents.

question: On a road without sidewalks a pedestrian should walk on which side?
options: a:The side facing oncoming traffic,b:The side on which traffic is moving (same side),c:The side with the lightest traffic
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see and react to approaching vehicles.

question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow for turn lanes?
options: a:Prepare to stop — a red arrow is coming unless you are already in the intersection,b:Merge immediately into the lane indicated by the arrow,c:Proceed without changing speed or position
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is imminent; stop unless you are already in the intersection and can safely complete your movement.

question: When passing a large truck, what should the driver of a small vehicle expect?
options: a:Gusts of wind from the large vehicle that may affect steering,b:Loud music from the truck's cabin,c:Extra pollution with no handling effects
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts capable of altering a small vehicle's direction; be prepared to countersteer if needed.

question: About how quickly does the average body process alcohol?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:One alcoholic drink per hour.,c:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.,d:Alcohol is processed instantly.
note: On average, the body eliminates roughly one standard drink per hour, though many individual factors affect this rate.

question: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop in the location under which condition?
options: a:To avoid conflict with other traffic,b:To unload packages for an extended time,c:To stop for any reason briefly
note: A 'No stopping' sign allows stopping only to obey traffic signals or to avoid a conflict with other traffic; otherwise stopping is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection, you must stop when you see which of these signals?
options: a:A flashing red light,b:A steady yellow light,c:A yellow arrow
note: A flashing red traffic signal means the same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: To practice defensive driving, you should:
options: a:Scan ahead for developing traffic situations, maintain proper following distance, and have alternate plans,b:Focus only on the car directly in front of you,c:Drive as slowly as possible at all times
note: Defensive driving requires looking well ahead, maintaining safe spacing, and preparing alternate maneuvers for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a required action when changing lanes?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.;b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes in residential areas.;c:Begin signaling after you start the lane change.;d:Ignore blind spots if mirrors look clear.
note: Before changing lanes in residential areas, begin signaling at least 100 feet ahead and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to clear the crossing faster.,c:Ignore warning signs if you do not see a train.
note: When you approach a railroad crossing, slow down, look for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning devices are activated, stop the required distance from the tracks.

question: What should you never allow when towing a trailer?
options: a:Have someone ride in the trailer to keep the load steady.,b:Allow only adults to ride in the trailer.,c:Never allow anyone to ride in the trailer.
note: Passengers should not ride in trailers; riding in trailers is prohibited and unsafe.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous and to be approached with caution,b:Generally safe to cross without stopping,c:Good places to park your car
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous; look and listen for trains and obey all signals and gates before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use your headlights.;b:Use hand signals.;c:Sound your horn.;d:Use your hazard lights instead.
note: If turn signals fail, use proper hand signals to show others when you intend to turn or change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a turn, what should you do?
options: a:Use your signal several seconds before the turn,b:Turn the wheel immediately,c:Increase your speed
note: Activate your turn signal three to four seconds before turning to alert others of your intention.

question: If you're in an accident and someone is injured, you should:
options: a:Not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid,b:Immediately move them away from the scene,c:Always leave the injured where they are without giving help
note: Unless there's immediate danger, avoid moving injured persons, keep them warm, and provide first aid while waiting for professional help.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign,b:A yield sign,c:A slow sign
note: Treat flashing red lights as stop signs: come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when safe.

question: Can prescription and over-the-counter medicines affect your driving?
options: a:Yes — many medicines can impair driving ability,b:No — only illegal drugs impair driving,c:Only medicines taken with alcohol have effects
note: Many medications, whether prescription or over-the-counter, can interfere with driving ability; consult your doctor about side effects.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.;b:Simply decline drinks when offered while at the event.;c:Call a taxi only after you feel intoxicated.;d:Drink lots of water while drinking alcohol.
note: Decide in advance that you will not drive if you plan to drink. Alcohol impairs judgment, making later decisions less reliable.

question: Which practice is safest when negotiating a curve?
options: a:Slow down on entry and gradually speed up on exit,b:Maintain the same speed from start to finish,c:Speed up entering and slow down when exiting
note: Approach curves slowly, then accelerate gradually as you exit to maintain control.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A deaf person.,b:A person involved with a traffic study.,c:A blind person.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the wheel straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas, then brake gently when under control,b:Brake hard immediately,c:Maintain speed and steer straight to the shoulder
note: Grip the wheel firmly, do not brake hard until you have control, ease off the accelerator, and pull off when safe.

question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren?
options: a:Only if it is behind you.;b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.;c:Regardless of which direction it is coming from, pull to the right and stop.;d:Only when you are in an intersection.
note: You must pull over to the right edge and stop for emergency vehicles using lights or sirens, regardless of the vehicle's direction of approach.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The middle of the intersection.;b:The right lane.;c:The left lane.;d:From the shoulder of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, start the turn from the left lane.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.,c:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,d:All of the above.
note: You must obey crossing gates and signals, not go around lowered gates, stop when directed by a flagger, and be aware that not all crossings have active warning devices.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:To stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:To run out in front of you without looking.
note: Children may not recognize danger and can run into the street unexpectedly, so slow down and use extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your car, you should:
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust speed to allow a safe pass,b:Pull off the road immediately,c:Signal when it is safe for them to pass while maintaining your lane position
note: When being passed, maintain steady speed, check for oncoming traffic, and adjust slightly if needed to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane safely.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians have no right-of-way.,d:Only yield if the pedestrian is in the center of the road.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are within a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady green light, what should you do?
options: a:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
note: A green light allows you to go but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection and be prepared to stop if the signal changes.

question: When driving in bad weather, what spacing adjustment should you make?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather.,d:Tailgate to prevent merging vehicles from cutting in.
note: In poor weather increase following distance to give yourself more time to react and stop safely.

question: When do roads become especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:The day following rainfall.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,d:Only when the temperature is below freezing.
note: Roads are often most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain as oil and residue rise to the surface, increasing skid risk.

question: A single broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is allowed when safe,b:Lanes moving in the same direction where passing is allowed,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions where passing is prohibited
note: A dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing when it is safe.

question: Which factors influence how alcohol affects a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach.;b:Body weight of the individual.;c:How much time passes between drinks.;d:All of the above.
note: BAC and impairment are affected by how much you drink, how fast, your weight, and whether you've eaten. Eating slows absorption slightly but doesn't prevent impairment.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road,b:Toward the right side of the road,c:Directly at the headlights
note: If another driver does not dim high beams, glance to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough view of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a speed limit sign posted on an exit ramp?
options: a:Reduce speed smoothly after you are in the exit lane to the posted limit,b:Regard the posted limit as merely a suggestion,c:Never drive slower than that posted speed on the ramp
note: Treat a posted speed limit on an exit ramp like any speed limit; slow down smoothly after you have moved into the exit lane.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection even when you have a green light; be especially cautious.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It helps you see side traffic more clearly.,d:It does not affect vision.
note: Higher speeds narrow your field of vision, so you must be more alert for hazards as speed increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.;b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before starting your turn.;c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you through.;d:Begin the turn into the first lane and then shift.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

question: How should drivers react to a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Increase their speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; reduce speed and proceed through the intersection carefully.

question: It is important to slow down in which situations?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections/railroad crossings, and when roads are wet or slippery,b:Only on freeways,c:Only in parking lots
note: Reduce speed on narrow/winding roads, near intersections and crossings, on hills and curves, where pedestrians/hazards exist, and when surfaces are slick.

question: The most important speed-management rule for curves is to:
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Drive the posted speed limit on entry and slow later,c:Accelerate gently before entering the curve
note: Because of inertia, you must reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control through the turn.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce your speed when roads are wet,b:Drive through deeper water to clear the tires,c:Increase speed to power through standing water
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds on wet surfaces; slow down to reduce the risk and maintain control.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct action?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.;b:Speed up and steer back on quickly.;c:Slow down, stay parallel to the road, and gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.;d:Immediately pull all the way off the road.
note: Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and when safe ease back onto the pavement while checking traffic.

question: The habit of turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes or merging is:
options: a:A good driving habit,b:Unnecessary,c:A bad driving habit
note: Physically checking blind spots by glancing over your shoulder is a proper habit that supplements mirror checks for safe lane changes.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line,b:Passing is permitted from either lane,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line
note: When a broken yellow line is adjacent to a solid yellow line, drivers next to the broken line may pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:When school bus lights are flashing.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:On a hill or curve.
note: You should never pass where your view is blocked, such as on a hill or curve, and in many other locations. Also, you may not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless there is a physical median.

question: Who is responsible for the mechanical condition of a vehicle you are driving?
options: a:The legal owner of the vehicle.,b:The garage mechanic.,c:The driver operating the vehicle.,d:The vehicle manufacturer.
note: The driver is responsible for ensuring the vehicle is in safe operating condition, regardless of ownership.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The recommended speed for bad weather.;b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.;c:The exact speed that guarantees you won't get a ticket.;d:A minimum safe speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. Drive more slowly when conditions require it.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, the best action is to:
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help,b:Get out and walk for help immediately,c:Lie down in the car and sleep
note: Remain in the vehicle where you are more likely to be found, conserve heat, and signal for help rather than venturing out in dangerous conditions.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) signs usually indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.;b:Pedestrian crossings.;c:School zones or school crossing areas.;d:Speed limits.
note: Pentagonal signs warn that you are in a school zone or near a school crossing; be alert for children and pedestrians.

question: What is the best way to deal with a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: If a vehicle is following you too closely, change lanes when safe or gradually slow down to let them pass rather than engaging in aggressive behavior.

question: Which behavior best describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring at objects off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.;b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation.;c:Only watching the vehicle directly ahead.;d:Checking mirrors regularly and scanning the road.
note: An inattentive driver is distracted by looking away from the road, daydreaming, or engaging in activities that divert attention from driving.

question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what is the correct response?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,d:Back up carefully to the exit.
note: Do not stop or reverse on the highway; continue to the next exit and safely turn around to return to your destination.

question: What must you have to drive a heavy truck in Hawaii?
options: a:Be at least 21 years old.,b:Have a valid driver license for the category of vehicle you wish to drive.,c:Have no special qualifications.
note: Drivers of large or commercial vehicles must hold the appropriate valid license class for the vehicle being driven.

question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, what should you generally do?
options: a:Enter slowly to avoid disrupting traffic.;b:Stop before merging to wait for a large gap.;c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge when safe.;d:Turn on your hazard lights until fully merged.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of highway traffic, signal, and merge into an appropriate gap.

question: If you approach an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived,b:Stop to watch and take pictures,c:Always stop even if it causes a traffic backup
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep moving while watching for pedestrians or hazards.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce your speed, and pull to a safe area to stop,b:Turn off the ignition immediately,c:Open your hood and inspect the engine while driving slowly
note: Loss of power steering requires extra steering effort; slow down, steer carefully to a safe area, and stop.

question: If you're in a hurry and must back into the street, you should first:
options: a:Check around the car for children and objects before backing,b:Honk loudly before reversing,c:Rev the engine to warn animals
note: Because backing has restricted visibility, always walk around and check for children, animals, and obstacles before reversing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, which blind-spot check should you make?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder, then signal.,b:Look over your right shoulder, then signal.,c:Look over both shoulders, then signal.,d:Check only your mirrors, no shoulder check required.
note: When moving right from the left lane, check your right blind spot by looking over your right shoulder, and signal before changing lanes.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,b:Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.,c:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point that drivers may appear intoxicated; simple measures like coffee or opening a window are insufficient to make a drowsy driver safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in rural areas.;b:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.;c:When traveling in heavy construction zones.;d:Never illegal to drive below the limit.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic can be unlawful. Keep pace with traffic while maintaining safety.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Stop and back up to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and leave there.,d:Pull over on the shoulder and reverse to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, go to the next exit and safely turn around. Do not back up or cross the median on the freeway.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:Allow the motorcyclist the right half of a traffic lane.,b:Allow the motorcyclist the entire width of a traffic lane.,c:Begin moving past the motorcycle before your vehicle is entirely in the passing lane.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane; give them plenty of space when passing.

question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
options: a:If you cannot move right, wait until clear and then slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass,b:Move quickly to the left lane to stop them,c:Brake sharply to warn them
note: If being tailgated and no right lane is available, wait for a clear stretch and gently reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass; never brake abruptly.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to those of smaller vehicles?
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots; trucks and large SUVs have areas that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.;b:Either driver may go first if they signal.;c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.;d:The driver that indicates first by hand signals has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving on a multilane highway and wish to change lanes, you must signal at least:
options: a:100 feet before the lane change,b:50 feet before the lane change,c:Immediately before changing lanes
note: Signals should be given for at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning; increase distance at higher speeds.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass a truck or bus regardless of conditions.;b:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate them.;c:Flash your lights to alert the driver.;d:Drive directly behind the truck to stay visible.
note: Avoid lingering alongside large vehicles and do not follow too closely; remain where the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: On slick roads, how should you negotiate turns and curves?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid curves.,c:Accelerate before turning to maintain momentum.,d:Use cruise control to maintain stability.
note: Reduce speed and take turns more slowly on slippery surfaces to reduce the chance of losing control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.;b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.;c:Drivers should make hand motions to communicate who goes first.;d:The larger vehicle must yield to the smaller one.
note: At a four-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

question: Bicyclists are required to:
options: a:Obey traffic laws, signs, and signals,b:Always ride on sidewalks in business districts,c:Ride in the center of traffic lanes regardless of conditions
note: Bicycles are vehicles under the law and must follow traffic signs, signals, and regulations like other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best general practice?
options: a:Enter slowly and wait for an opening.;b:Stop at the end of the ramp, then merge.;c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.;d:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.
note: Use acceleration lanes to reach the speed of freeway traffic so you can blend smoothly and safely into the travel lane.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:Because they are blind,b:Because they are likely to be deaf,c:Because they are a traffic officer
note: A white cane or guide dog usually indicates the pedestrian is blind; slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop to avoid injury.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed.,b:Wait for the green light.,c:Proceed as directed by the officer.
note: You must obey lawful directions from police officers even if they conflict with traffic signals.

question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate:
options: a:No passing allowed from either direction,b:Passing is allowed for both directions,c:Passing is allowed at hilltops only
note: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that indicate?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic; a broken yellow indicates a two-way road where passing is allowed when safe.

question: What happens to your tires on a wet road as your speed increases?
options: a:They become less effective at clearing water.,b:Good tires eliminate any danger from water.,c:Deep water is always safer than shallow water.,d:Speed has no effect on traction.
note: As speed increases on wet pavement, tires lose their ability to clear water and can hydroplane, losing traction.

question: Worn or bald tires can:
options: a:Increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and raise hydroplaning risk,b:Make turning easier,c:Reduce the chance of hydroplaning
note: Insufficient tire tread increases stopping distance, decreases traction in turns, and heightens hydroplaning risk.

question: What type of sign warns drivers about potential hazards ahead?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions; obey them to avoid accidents.

question: If stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer to approach, preparing paperwork when asked,b:Unbuckle and step out immediately,c:Lower your window and get out before the officer arrives
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands on the wheel, have passengers keep hands visible, and wait until the officer requests documents.

question: If two vehicles are side by side ahead of you and you are in a hurry, what should you do?
options: a:Tailgate the vehicle in the left lane and flash headlights.,b:Drive directly behind the right-lane vehicle to push it.,c:Maintain at least a two-second following interval in whichever lane you choose.,d:Swerve between lanes to advance.
note: Always maintain a safe following distance (at least two seconds) regardless of being in a hurry; do not tailgate or force other vehicles to yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Has the right-of-way.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and yield to vehicles already on the interstate before merging.

question: When is it lawful to drink alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:If you are not the driver.;b:When riding in the back seat.;c:If you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.;d:It is illegal to consume or possess an alcoholic beverage on a public road or sidewalk in areas normally occupied by passengers.
note: It is unlawful to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages on public roads; storing an open container in areas normally occupied by driver or passengers is prohibited.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow means proceed with caution; scan carefully and yield as needed.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed gradually, keep wheels off pavement until safe, then steer gently back on,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force back onto pavement,c:Slam on brakes immediately
note: Remain calm, slow gradually while keeping wheels off pavement, and steer back onto the road when at a safe speed to avoid losing control.

question: Where should you keep a copy of your vehicle inspection certificate?
options: a:Should be filed with your income tax return.,b:Should be kept in a safe place in your home.,c:Should be kept in the vehicle.
note: After a periodic motor vehicle inspection, one copy of the inspection certificate must remain in the vehicle.

question: When a traffic signal displays a green arrow for a turn, what does it mean?
options: a:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,b:You may proceed only in the direction of the arrow even if the circular light is red.,c:You may go straight regardless of the arrow.,d:The arrow only applies to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow allows movement only in the direction indicated by the arrow; it has priority even if the circular light is red.

question: What practice can help you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk to alert other drivers.;b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.;c:Drive only in the right lane.;d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to push them along.
note: By scanning ahead and keeping a safe following distance, you can anticipate hazards and avoid sudden emergency stops.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition in your car?
options: a:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and see that all passengers do likewise.
note: Develop a routine: before turning on the ignition, fasten your seat belt and ensure all passengers are properly restrained.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train.,c:Look for a train, then speed up if none are visible.
note: If warning signals are flashing at a crossing, stop your vehicle no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait for the train to pass.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) typically painted?
options: a:In curves and on hills.;b:Next to churches and schools.;c:Across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.;d:At bus stops only.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks to show where drivers must stop.

question: If you change your address, when and how must you notify the county examiner of drivers?
options: a:In writing within 30 days.,b:In writing within 10 days.,c:In person within 10 days.,d:By phone within 30 days.
note: You must notify the county examiner in writing of your new address, name, and license number within 30 days of an address change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At intersections.,b:On hills and curves.,c:At railroad crossings.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills and curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings where visibility or safety is compromised.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, you should:
options: a:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway if it is safe to do so,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances,c:Wait for the police before moving the vehicle
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle out of the travel lanes if possible; do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and rendering aid if needed.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The right side of the road,b:The center of the road,c:Either side of the road
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining enough roadway in view to stay on course.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left but oncoming traffic is heavy, what should you do while the light is green?
options: a:Enter the intersection to prepare for the turn and wait for a safe gap,b:Wait in the crosswalk until traffic clears,c:Use the next intersection instead
note: If the light is green you may enter the intersection to prepare for a left turn and wait there for a safe gap, provided you do not block crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before you pass, check your mirrors, signal, check your blind spots, then pass only when it is safe.

question: If the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.
note: When the broken line is on your side of the centerline, you may pass when it is safe because your side permits passing.

question: How is driving much slower than the speed limit generally viewed?
options: a:It is always the safest option.,b:It always gives you the right-of-way.,c:It can be hazardous and you may need to let others pass.,d:You should never let following cars pass you.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous; on two-lane roads, if traffic backs up, you must pull over and let others pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.,d:The vehicle with faster speed.
note: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A steady green arrow permits you to proceed in the arrow's direction; oncoming traffic is stopped for turning traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Ensure the lane you intend to use is clear before you move over,b:Always pass only on the right,c:Assume oncoming traffic will yield
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, confirm the passing lane is clear and signal your lane change.

question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and lights, what is true?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way to it,b:You may ignore it if you are in a hurry,c:You must always follow it closely
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights, and follow any instructions given over loudspeaker.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,c:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed when safe.

question: A brake warning lamp on the instrument panel typically indicates:
options: a:The brake system may be defective if it illuminates while pressing the foot brake,b:It should come on when the parking brake is released,c:It will never come on
note: The brake warning lamp should extinguish after releasing the parking brake; if it lights when applying the foot brake, the brake system may be defective and the vehicle shouldn't be driven.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,c:Release the gas and let the vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,d:All of the above.
note: Avoid sudden stops, check mirrors and blind spots, and ease off the accelerator to slow before braking to reduce rear-end collision risk.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Approach cautiously and cross only after confirming no trains are coming,b:Turn your radio down to listen for a train,c:Proceed only when a flagger clears you
note: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only after ensuring no train is approaching from either direction; obey any flagger if present.

question: When sleet or snow begins, you should:
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance,b:Drive at posted highway speeds without change,c:Approach vehicles more closely to monitor them
note: In snowy or icy conditions keep windows clear and allow extra stopping distance because slippery roads increase stopping distances.

question: When driving in fog, which actions should you take?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights for better illumination.;b:Drive cautiously, reduce speed, and use low beam headlights.;c:Turn off your headlights to avoid glare.;d:Speed up to leave the foggy area quickly.
note: In foggy conditions drive cautiously at reduced speed and use low beams (or fog lights) because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, you should:
options: a:Assume someone may open a door and use extra caution,b:Speed up to pass quickly,c:Slam on your brakes
note: Expect doors to open and pedestrians to appear; slow and give extra space when passing parked cars.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate that drivers must yield to trains.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes, if you hurry.;b:No, it is not legal to cross double solid yellow lines to pass.;c:Yes, but only at night.;d:Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: You may not cross double solid yellow lines to pass. Crossing is allowed only to turn into or out of a driveway or entrance where permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane,b:Before entering the deceleration lane,c:Only after you see the toll booth
note: Move into the exit lane well before the ramp and then reduce speed smoothly once you are in the exit lane.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path, and stop when safe.,d:Speed up to get away from the emergency vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching, slow, yield a clear path by moving aside if safe, and stop to let it pass.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up to deter them.,d:Confront them by blocking their path.
note: Give an aggressive driver space and avoid eye contact or retaliation; do your best to let them pass safely.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian by law.;b:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.;c:Whoever started moving last.;d:Whoever is slower.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even at intersections without traffic lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, you should generally ____ your speed.
options: a:Vary by slowing to maintain control,b:Increase speed,c:Maintain speed
note: Reduce speed as needed to maintain control, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations while turning.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Blow the horn repeatedly.,b:Slam on the brakes until it stops.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Turn off the ignition carefully, apply brakes, and steer to a safe area to stop.
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition only enough to stop the engine without locking the steering, apply brakes, and move to a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles to get out of your way.;b:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.;c:Honk your horn to alert others.;d:Merge quickly without stopping if traffic looks light.
note: Always stop before entering a roadway from a driveway and yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, what sequence of looking should you use before proceeding?
options: a:Look right, then left, then right again.,b:Look left first, then right, then left again.,c:Only check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.,d:Wait for the car ahead to move before looking.
note: When stopped, first look left, then right, then left again to ensure no vehicles or hazards are approaching.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe,b:Lanes move in opposite directions,c:Drivers may not pass
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line permits lane changes or passing when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing another vehicle illegal?
options: a:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.,d:None of the above.
note: You may not pass on hills or in curves where visibility is limited, by driving onto the shoulder, or where solid lines prohibit passing.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates:
options: a:Stop,b:Speed limit,c:Hospital ahead
note: Eight-sided (octagonal) signs are always stop signs; come to a full stop when you encounter one.
