question: Which sections of road are most likely to freeze first in cold, wet weather?
options: a:Flat sections of roadway.,b:Shaded sections of roadway.,c:Roads that are in the sun.
note: Areas shaded by trees or buildings tend to freeze before exposed sections and are often the last to dry after precipitation.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.;b:Keep driving in your lane until it passes.;c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.;d:Speed up and get out of its way by any lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, safely pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving?
options: a:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications,b:Only illegal drugs,c:Only prescription drugs
note: Many kinds of drugs — legal prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal substances — can impair driving ability.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:May still turn in that direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:No longer may turn and must go straight,c:Keep the right-of-way to turn
note: When a green arrow ends, you may complete the turn but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic if required.

question: Which of the following is least likely to occur after drinking?
options: a:Your judgment is distorted,b:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down,c:None of these — alcohol causes all of them
note: Alcohol reduces reaction time, impairs judgment and perception of speed and distance, and decreases alertness — all are effects of drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow roadway when meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road,b:Stop immediately and honk your horn,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over
note: On narrow roads, each vehicle should leave sufficient space; allow the other vehicle at least half the traveled portion to pass safely.

question: What minimum following interval should you leave behind the vehicle ahead?
options: a:One second.;b:Two seconds.;c:100 feet.;d:Five seconds.
note: To reduce the risk of rear-end collisions, leave at least a two-second following interval under normal driving conditions.

question: A vehicle using emergency signals is approaching from the opposite direction on a two-lane street. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard it because it is coming the other way.;b:Stop as quickly as you can in your lane.;c:Slow down, move as far to the right as possible, and stop.;d:Try to outrun it to clear the way.
note: On a two-lane street, slow down and pull as far right as possible and stop to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.;b:Honk continuously to scare it off.;c:Pass the animal as closely as possible to get by quickly.;d:Maintain speed and expect the animal to move.
note: Be very cautious around animals on the road. Slow down and pass slowly so you don't frighten or startle the animal.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:Have large blind spots.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop than passenger cars.

question: Orange traffic signs most commonly indicate what?
options: a:Regulatory requirements.;b:School zone areas.;c:Work zones and road construction ahead.;d:General information.
note: Orange signs with black symbols or letters typically warn of highway work zones and that people or equipment may be on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street unless you:
options: a:Can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic,b:Have the legal right to pass regardless of visibility,c:Are driving the fastest vehicle on the road
note: To pass safely on a two-lane road you must be able to see clearly ahead and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle and check before getting in to reverse,b:Only use rearview mirrors while reversing,c:Honk immediately before shifting into reverse
note: Before backing, exit and inspect behind your vehicle for children and objects; mirrors alone may not reveal all hazards.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires adjusting your driving.,b:You should slow down in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.,d:All of the above.
note: Sudden weather changes require adjustments: slow down in rain or fog and watch for other vehicles that may not slow appropriately.

question: If a trailer blocks your internal rearview mirror, what is required?
options: a:Install an outside mirror on the driver's side.,b:Install an outside mirror on the passenger side.,c:Add outside rearview mirrors on both sides of the towing vehicle.,d:Remove the trailer.
note: If a trailer obstructs the inside mirror, you must install properly sized outside rearview mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.

question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do to reduce crash risk?
options: a:Use alternate routes only.;b:Drive as you would on dry roads.;c:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time.;d:Brake harder to stop sooner.
note: On slippery roads increase your following distance because it takes longer to stop than under normal conditions.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke affect driving?
options: a:It does not affect driving ability.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity.,d:It improves focus on the road.
note: Smoking and handling smoking materials are distractions that can take your hands and eyes off driving tasks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign show?
options: a:Only a suggested driving speed.;b:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.;c:The one speed that prevents all crashes.;d:The maximum speed in poor weather.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. Slow down when conditions (weather, traffic) require it.

question: What driving practice helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Anticipating traffic and slowing gradually instead of braking and accelerating frequently reduces fuel consumption.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard,c:Assume the crossing guard may be ignored
note: Obey crossing guards and posted signs in school zones; be prepared to reduce speed and take extra care for children.

question: What name is given to signs that drivers must obey?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs display laws and rules that drivers must follow; failure to obey can result in penalties.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:They are making quick and sudden stops.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, erratic lane changes, sudden braking, and inconsistent speeds.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, how should you prepare?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs mean slow down, look, and be prepared to stop for approaching trains; never go around lowered gates.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that workers may be present,b:That it is summer and paving season,c:You must immediately stop and back up
note: Orange work zone signs warn of road work ahead; reduce speed and be prepared for changes and workers near the roadway.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop driving and rest,b:Open a window or get coffee and keep going,c:Turn up the radio volume
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; stop and rest or switch drivers rather than continuing while drowsy.

question: When driving on public streets or highways, you must:
options: a:Have and show your driver license to law enforcement upon request,b:Only have a license at home,c:Be able to recite your license number from memory
note: You must carry a valid driver license while operating a vehicle and present it to an officer when requested.

question: What is the best way to reduce your chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy,b:Watch out for standing water or puddles,c:Keep your tires properly maintained
note: To avoid hydroplaning, maintain proper tire condition and pressure, reduce speed in wet conditions, and avoid standing water when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right,b:The vehicle on the left,c:The larger vehicle
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: When are you allowed to go around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Under no circumstances,b:After the lights stop flashing and the train has passed,c:When you hear the train but see no cars on the tracks
note: Never drive around lowered crossing gates; wait until signals indicate it is safe and the gates are fully raised.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When emergency vehicle sirens are heard, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow them to pass.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning, you should:
options: a:Maintain good tire tread and proper inflation and reduce speed in the rain,b:Only ensure tires are properly inflated,c:Only reduce speed when puddles appear
note: Good tread and correct tire pressure plus reducing speed in wet conditions greatly reduce hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:One driver may continue driving without stopping.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an open intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When changing lanes, how should you check blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to view the blind spot,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror,c:Rely solely on outside mirrors
note: A head check over the shoulder is required to confirm the blind spot is clear before a lane change.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on drivers?
options: a:It increases reflexes and reaction time.,b:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,c:It makes drivers more alert.,d:It only affects mood, not driving skills.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reduces reaction time, and impairs driving skills necessary for safe operation.

question: When you park facing downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.;b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.;c:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).;d:Turn your wheels toward the center of the road.
note: On a downhill slope, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road so that if your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the children.,b:Rev the engine briefly to gain attention.,c:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to ensure the way is clear.,d:Back out slowly while watching through the rearview mirror.
note: Before reversing where children may be present, get out and check behind the vehicle; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: A driver taking an over-the-counter (non-prescription) medication should:
options: a:Read labels and heed warnings before driving,b:Drink alcohol to offset drowsiness,c:Ignore labels and continue driving
note: Many OTC medications can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about driving while medicated.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Is never used as a traffic signal.,c:Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.
note: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light: traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.

question: If your car begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go,b:To keep the front wheels straight,c:In the opposite direction of the skid
note: Correct skid recovery is to steer into the direction you want the car to move until control returns, then straighten the wheel.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle trunk to improve traction.;b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.;c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.;d:Engage four-wheel drive and maintain normal following distances.
note: Reducing speed and increasing the distance between you and the vehicle ahead are the most important techniques for safe driving on snow or ice.

question: Which of the following may you legally install on your private vehicle?
options: a:A blue light visible outside of the vehicle.,b:A bell, exhaust whistle, or siren.,c:A muffler cut-out or by-pass.,d:None of the above.
note: It is illegal to add equipment such as exterior blue lights, bells/exhaust whistles/sirens, or muffler cut-outs that alter the vehicle's original safety equipment or mimic emergency vehicles.

question: Which traffic signal situation corresponds to stopping, yielding to cross traffic/pedestrians, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A solid green light
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.;b:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.;c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.;d:Recommended speeds only for novice drivers.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down for adverse conditions as necessary.
